messages:
jamal: Heads up — nightly long-seq job spiked. Throughput for 4096 token run down ~18%. Perfetto timeline shows rapid HBM read bursts and a flurry of KV page evictions.

perf-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression detected: long-seq throughput -18% vs baseline at 1804129999 :warning:

alex: Which build/commit landed before the run? can you drop the nsys and nvprof links and a quick top-line kernel breakdown?

jamal: commit 9c3d1f8 went in ~1804126000 (kernel selector revamp). Perf captures: perfetto trace s3://rwd-perf/traces/1804129999, nsys output at /tmp/nsys_longseq. nvprof top results I parsed:
```
memcpy_async      45.7%   (heavy HBM transfer)
sgemm_fp16        28.9%   (fell back to fp32 on long seq)
attention_mm      10.2%
```

lina: initial guess: new selector chooses a fallback kernel path for seq >= 2048 that increases HBM traffic and leads to larger microbatches; combined with our KV-page eviction policy this creates a thrash loop.

maria: seeing same effect on staging-proxy. P95 latency for 4096 moves 220ms -> 360ms intermittently. Traces show the same prefix being fetched from KV multiple times within 8-12ms windows.

alex: can we reproduce locally with the synthetic harness? run with --kv-trace and sprof sampling, capture nsys with mem+cuda categories.

jamal: repro command I used:
```
./perf_harness --model rwd-l2 --seq 4096 --concurrency 8 --microbatch auto --kv-trace=1 --sprof
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_longseq --trace=cuda,mem,osrt ./perf_harness ...
```

perf-bot: KV metrics snapshot: read bandwidth +4.6x, eviction rate +2.0x during regression window.

lina: timeline shows repeated memcpy_async spikes that line up with KV page load events. HBM utilization bursts to ~92% during those stamps, and kernels stall waiting on memory.

alex: looks like two potential fixes: (A) reduce duplicate KV page fetches (prefetch, coalesce, or transient locks), (B) make selector prefer lower-bandwidth kernels for long sequences or incorporate bandwidth into cost model.

jamal: quick patch: if seq >= 2048, force quantized kernel path and cap microbatch to 4; also added a transient in-flight fetch dedupe for KV pages. Prototype pushed to my branch.

maria: alternative: implement request coalescing in the fronting router — collapse identical prefix requests within 5ms so only one backend fetch happens. That would lower duplicate KV reads without tweaking kernel heuristics.

lina: that helps, but the selector still falls back to fp32 path when HBM latency spikes. The selector currently uses steady-state bandwidth estimates; we should add short-window HBM tail latency/eviction signals to its decision vector.

alex: tactical plan: revert the selector change from 9c3d1f8 to stabilize, deploy KV fetch dedupe as a mitigation, then iterate on selector telemetry. Rollback gets us closest to baseline in quick tests.

jamal: microbench numbers:
- baseline: 1000 tok/s
- post-change regressed: 820 tok/s
- dedupe + microbatch cap: 900 tok/s
- revert selector: 995 tok/s

maria: starting canary with revert + dedupe now. will monitor HBM read bandwidth, eviction counters, and perfetto traces. Canary started at 1804130200.

perf-bot: canary monitor armed at 1804130200. Will fire if throughput drop >5% vs baseline.

alex: next actions: (1) revert commit in main & PR revert, (2) add KV fetch coalescing at routing layer and lightweight per-page in-flight lock, (3) extend selector cost model to include recent HBM bandwidth and eviction rate, (4) add long-seq nsys sampling into our CI perf gate.

lina: I'll draft RFC for selector telemetry and a perf matrix: seq lengths 1024/2048/4096, microbatch sizes 1-8, concurrency sweep. Also propose adding a short-window HBM tail-lat metric to our telemetry pipeline.

jamal: uploaded raw perf artifacts and nvprof CSV to s3://rwd-perf/1804129999/ and attached perfetto slices here.

maria: thanks. I'll report back after 90 minutes of canary traffic with charts.

alex: thanks team. If revert stabilizes, we should ship the coalesce/dedupe patch quickly and schedule the selector telemetry work. :thumbsup:

jamal: will follow up with a brief postmortem and the repro steps. ping me if you want the local nsys capture copy.
